title: Adaptive attention kernel selector + prefill/decode scheduler for FlashAttention v3
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: build an adaptive kernel selection layer that picks between FlashAttention v2, FlashAttention v3, and our fallback attention implementation at runtime, and decouple prefill vs decode scheduling to avoid regressions for short-sequence low-latency requests. This ticket tracks design, experiments, implementation, canary rollout, and observability additions. Motivation: FA3 shows strong throughput for long sequences but we observed decode latency regressions for many customer workloads composed of short-turn conversations and small batch sizes.
comments: 2025-11-03 — Aisha: Created ticket after triage meeting. Root cause hypothesis: FA3 has larger kernel launch overhead and different workspace allocation patterns that hurt sub-64 token decode latency and high-concurrency workloads. FA3 still wins for prefill-heavy requests at seq_len >= 512.

2025-11-05 — Marco: Ran microbench harness across T4, A10G, and H100. Summary: FA3 decode p50 improved by 12% at seq_len=1024, but p50 worsened by 18% at seq_len=32. Prefill throughput improved consistently for long context. Attached raw CSV to artifacts.

2025-11-07 — Marco: Implemented a simple heuristic prototype in the runtime: if (seq_len >= 256 OR batch_size >= 8) use FA3; else use FA2 or fallback. Microbench shows this recovers short-seq regressions but misses some mid-range shapes. Need more robust cost model.

2025-11-09 — Eng team sync: Decided to separate prefill and decode scheduling decisions. Prefill can use larger workspace/throughput-optimized kernels (favor FA3), decode should bias toward low-launch-overhead kernels for small token counts (favor FA2 or minimal fused attention).

2025-11-10 — Marco: Added telemetry hooks: kernel_choice_reason tag, seq_len, batch_size, kv_cache_present, hardware_type, wall_ms. Plan: collect 2 weeks of canary traffic for model:open/fast-chat and model:open/long-context.

2025-11-12 — QA: Found regression in beam search path when switching kernels mid-request (prefill used FA3, decode used FA2): KV cache alignment differences caused off-by-one token artefacts in some models. Root cause traced to workspace padding / qk scaling ordering mismatch between kernels.

2025-11-13 — Marco: Hotfix: enforce consistent normalization and padding rules in the kernel selection shim so KV cache layout is invariant to kernel choice. Added unit tests that compare outputs with reference FP32 attention for 8 random seeds across seq_len 16..2048.

2025-11-15 — Performance lead (Diego): Collected canary metrics on dedicated pool (2000 requests): overall median latency improved by 6% for mixed workload, tail (p95) improved by 3%. Short-seq (<=64) p50 recovered to baseline. Cost estimate: FA3 route reduces token compute cost by ~9% on H100 for long contexts but increases CPU overhead for kernel negotiation at high concurrency — need to quantify in production traffic.

2025-11-16 — PM (Sana): Ask: expose kernel selector as an opt-in route-level config in Dedicated so customers can pin behavior per-model. Also request fallback telemetry surfaced in Console rollout bar and per-model dashboards.

2025-11-17 — Marco: Next steps: 1) Finalize cost model (empirical latency + compute cost) and replace heuristics with small decision table. 2) Run 48h canary on hosted-small and dedicated medium pools. 3) Add RPC-level contract tests to prevent KV layout regressions. 4) Prepare rollout playbook and abort criteria (if short-seq p95 increases >5% or error-rate >0.2%).
notes: Important constraints: all outputs must bitwise-match reference for canary until we validate quantized kernels. Regression mitigation path must be sub-second rollout. Keep flamegraph and kernel timeline traces for every failed canary request.
